text:
maria: Quick q — where should we parse org/project/service-account claims from API keys: at the edge router or in the auth-proxy? This changes telemetry, quota attribution, and routing. cc @ryan
ryan: leaning auth-proxy. keeps the router simple and avoids duplicating verification logic. but auth-proxy adds a few ms of latency and is a single point for attribution. :thinking:
sophie: If the router parses, we can tag requests earlier which helps routing/pinning and reduces tail in some flows. downside: duplicate code and more places that need key material or verification logic.
maria: duplication is the main worry. we'd need a shared verifier lib, or the router would call out to auth-proxy (which defeats the point latency-wise). Also we need token fields surfaced to console for billing dashboards.
jonathan: Telemetry angle — router currently emits origin headers only. auth-proxy emits full claims but we sample heavily. If router can do best-effort parsing (no revocation checks) we could get 100% attribution for routing and early metrics.
ryan: numbers matter here. auth-proxy adds ~3-6ms p95 on our tests. Router budget is tighter (we aim <8ms hop), but router already touches raw headers so parsing might be cheap if we avoid crypto ops.
sophie: security note: verifying signed tokens usually requires public keys only (for JWT) which is fine. revocation / allowlist checks need a call to auth-proxy or K/V store. Router should not hold KMS secrets.
maria: proposal draft: ship a small public-key-only verifier module to the router (best-effort). Router extracts and emits claims as provisional attributes used for routing/telemetry. The auth-proxy performs canonical verification (exp, revocations, org-state) and emits canonical attribution that overrides router provisional tags.
ryan: that compromise makes sense. need a plan for disagreement periods: router provisional != auth-proxy final. Console and dashboards need to show source and confidence (e.g., attributed_by: router|auth-proxy, confidence: low|high).
deploy-bot: deploy-staging: verifier-lib v0.2 deployed to router-staging, traffic 5% — see https://ci.internal/release/1245
sophie: also think about delegated tokens / impersonation. Router best-effort parse might see the delegate SA but not the 'actor' chain. auth-proxy has full context and may attribute to the delegator. Console UX should show both: primary actor + effective principal.
maria: ok action items: I'll write a short RFC describing the verifier lib API + rollout plan. @ryan please bench auth-proxy p95 with verifier off/on (EOD). @sophie mock console "attribution" panel with both provisional vs canonical flags. i'll prototype verifier lib (public-key only) and unit tests. :thumbsup:
ryan: ack
